facts.text: I have a lump in my neck.
It's on the right side of my neck.

facts.item: how long the neck lump and cough have lasted

facts.text: It's a dry cough; nothing comes up.
It comes on now and then, not all the time.
It comes in severe coughing fits.

facts.item: cough: triggered by pressing on the neck lump
facts.text: Pressing on the lump in my neck sets off the cough every time.

facts.item: cough: brought on by eating, talking or moving
facts.text: Eating, talking or moving doesn't bring it on.
The coughing fits sometimes make me throw up.
My voice goes hoarse on and off.

facts.item: food or drink coming back through the nose, or a nasal voice
facts.text: Food and drink don't come back up through my nose, and my voice doesn't sound nasal.
I don't have any medical problems.
Nobody in my family has had a neuroendocrine tumour.

findings.name: neck examination
findings.result: 2.5-cm right-sided level II neck mass deep to the sternocleidomastoid muscle; discrete, mobile and nonpulsatile; palpation immediately triggers coughing.

findings.name: general physical examination
findings.result: Unremarkable except for a mildly hoarse voice.

findings.name: flexible fiberoptic laryngoscopy
findings.result: Normal true vocal-fold appearance and movement bilaterally; only prominent retropharyngeal carotid arteries noted.

findings.name: CT angiography of the neck
findings.result: 2.4 × 2.2 × 2.2-cm heterogeneously enhancing, irregular mass in the right carotid sheath lateral to the proximal internal and external carotid arteries, with minimal arterial splaying and a central area of lower attenuation suggestive of necrosis.

findings.name: MRI of the neck
aliases: magnetic resonance imaging of the neck
findings.result: 2.5 × 1.9 × 3.0-cm mass within the carotid sheath, extending from the inferior margin of the right carotid to the level of the piriform sinuses, enhancing intensely after contrast administration.

gold.reasoning: 1. Vagal paraganglioma remained in the differential given the mass’s location and enhancement — “Differential diagnoses included vagal paraganglioma, schwannoma, neurofibroma, or a necrotic lymph node.” 2. Neurofibroma was considered among neurogenic tumors of the carotid sheath — “Differential diagnoses included … neurofibroma …” 3. A necrotic lymph node was included due to central low attenuation on CT — “Differential diagnoses included … a necrotic lymph node.”

quotes.f003: a 4-week history of a right-sided neck mass and a sporadic dry cough
quotes.f008: was reproducibly triggered by palpation of the neck mass
quotes.f009: unrelated to eating, talking, or movement
quotes.f015: no family history of neuroendocrine tumors

f008: The source says palpation of the mass triggers the cough; worded as what the patient would notice when the lump is pressed.
f013: 'Denied velopharyngeal insufficiency' rendered in lay terms as no nasal regurgitation and no nasal voice, the two complaints the term covers.

source_issues: s009 says 'laboratory studies, including' a blood panel and urinary catecholamines were normal; any other laboratory tests are not named, so only these two are findings.
notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation with a 4-week right-sided neck mass and dry cough (s001-s011; all examinations and tests belong to that workup).

The cough's attributes (dry, sporadic, severe fits, triggered by pressing the lump, not triggered by eating, talking or movement) are child facts; post-tussive vomiting is its own symptom so that 'any vomiting?' finds it.
The intermittent hoarseness is a patient fact; the examiner's 'mildly hoarse voice' stays in the general examination finding.
'Medical history was unremarkable' is one 'chronic medical problems' absent fact.
